C-44, ss. 21.1–21.5 (register of individuals with significant control); Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, s. 29 (register of beneficial owners); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and associated FINTRAC Regulations (SOR/2002-184 et seq.); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — Federal register of individuals with significant control is non-public and accessible to FINTRAC, Canada Revenue Agency, law enforcement, and financial institution compliance units; Quebec REQ register contains partially public UBO declarations; not nominee-friendly where the nominee merely holds title, as statutory language requires disclosure of true beneficial ownership

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and signatories against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Magnitsky Act, and OFAC SDN list where required by Canadian Schedule I clearing banks; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for non-resident UBOs and politically exposed persons under FINTRAC reporting and ongoing monitoring obligations, with source-of-funds verification required for all equity injection into the holding SPV

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada NUANS Online (https://ised-isde.canada.ca); Provincial: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) — name searches must be executed through a certified NUANS search house or the REQ online search service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, the name of a Quebec-registered business corporation must be in French; a name in another language may only be used with a French parallel form and prior approval of the Office québécois de la langue française where the enterprise is provincially incorporated; statutory French corporate designations ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée') satisfy transliteration requirements; the Latin alphabet is required; federal CBCA names may be in English, French, or both, but a French name version is required for active operational presence in Quebec
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying regulatory status, sovereignty, or public office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Federal: file an extension request with Corporations Canada within the reservation window (extendable by up to 60 days upon payment of the applicable fee); upon final refusal by the Director under s. 12 CBCA, file written submissions for administrative reconsideration, then seek judicial review before the Federal Court under s. 18 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7. Quebec: submit a written reconsideration application to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 60 days of the refusal, pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; final recourse lies to the Court of Québec.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as sole registered office — Quebec law requires a physical, verifiable place of business in Quebec where corporate records are kept and service of process can be made during normal business hours; a P.O. box or mail-forwarding virtual address may serve as an ancillary correspondence address but cannot satisfy the statutory head office requirement; federal CBCA corporations must maintain a registered office in the province of the head office with a physical street address
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-Elevated — REQ and CRA conduct unannounced verification of registered offices and premises in approximately 10% of newly incorporated entities annually; purely passive equity holding SPVs with no employee presence, no fixed assets, and no CRA filings within the first 12 months face a 30% probability of on-site inspection over a three-year window and a higher risk of CRA GAAR audit under s. 245 of the Income Tax Act for lack of commercial substance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (Quebec Business Corporations Act), ss. 9-25 (incorporation and articles), s. 20 (registered office), s. 58 (first directors), s. 69 (by-laws)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar, online portal and registry office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution), form AR-1, filed electronically with the REQ
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration. If par value shares are adopted, the consideration received must be at least equal to the aggregate par value, which is fully credited to stated capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for a business corporation incorporated in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED:

1. The incorporator subscribes for 100 common shares at the designated issuance price, receipt whereof is acknowledged, and directs the directors to issue the shares to the sole shareholder upon payment in full.

2. The registered office of the Corporation is established at the principal address in Québec identified in the Articles, subject to relocation by directors upon filing.

3. The undersigned constitute the first board of directors, who shall appoint officers, adopt by-laws, open bank accounts, and complete filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to activate the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary availability check in the REQ enterprise register, then submit a name reservation request (Requête de réservation de nom) through the REQ online portal. The proposed name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.'), and must comply with the Charter of the French Language by being expressed in French or in bilingual form. Pay the reservation fee; the reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form completed online
Identity and contact details of the incorporator
Proposed corporate name compliant with Quebec language law
Declaration of intended activity (passive equity holding)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, file an amended name reservation within the notice period citing the REQ notification, propose a revised distinctive element, and resubmit; the incorporator may also convert to a numbering name or use the legal name in both French and English form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit form AR-1 'Constitution d'une personne morale' electronically through the REQ platform, entering the reserved name reference, the registered office physical address in Quebec (no post-office box), the first directors' names and residential addresses, and the authorized share structure, including classes of shares and any restriction on transfer applicable to a private holding corporation. Pay the statutory filing fee by credit card, debit, or pre-authorized account.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate number
Form AR-1 executed by the incorporator
Registered office address in Quebec
First directors' identification data
Authorized share structure and class rights description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a deficiency notice from REQ, correct the flagged fields and resubmit within the cure period indicated in the notice; if the articles are rejected without constitutive effect, a corrected version may be refiled without additional fee when submitted within the applicable statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Directors' Consents and Registered Office Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain signed consent-to-act forms (Consentement de l'administrateur) from each first director and confirm the registered office address. The consent must be delivered to the REQ with the articles or immediately after filing; directors must be natural persons of full capacity, and a majority of directors must be Canadian residents or, for a Quebec corporation, resident in Canada per statutory quorum rules.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director signed by each director
Registered office address proof (lease or municipal documentation)
Directors' addresses and dates of birth
Statement of director residency for quorum purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a consent is rejected for incompleteness, obtain corrected signatures and file a declaration of rectification with REQ, updating the director roster retroactive to the date of incorporation if permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the articles, REQ issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and assigns the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). The corporation exists as of the certificate date. Verify the REQ register entry online, obtain a certified extract (extrait du registre), and confirm the legal designation, registered office, and director information listed in the public record.
required_dossiers: REQ payment receipt
Approved articles of incorporation
NEQ allocation notice
Request for certified enterprise register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register entry contains errors, file a declaration of rectification (déclaration rectificative) with REQ within the statutory period; request an expedited certified extract if banking or licensing counter-parties demand immediate proof of existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the initial registration of the enterprise with Revenu Québec through its online business service to obtain the Quebec enterprise number, and determine whether a QST account (TVQ), source deductions account, or GST/HST account is required. For a pure equity holding corporation, optional registration may apply; maintain passive status by collecting and reporting dividends properly. File the initial return (Déclaration initiale) within 60 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
Articles of incorporation
Directors' identification and social insurance numbers
Ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure
Description of passive dividend-holding activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or CRA queries the registration, submit a letter explaining the intermediate holding company structure, confirm the absence of employees or taxable commercial activity, and provide the REQ extract; amend the initial return promptly to avoid penalty assessments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors under the Business Corporations Act (Québec) and REQ public register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting; adopt the corporation's by-laws (règlements intérieurs); issue share certificates for the subscribed shares; elect or appoint officers (president, secretary, treasurer); open corporate bank accounts using the certificate of incorporation, NEQ extract, board resolution, and directors' identification. Maintain statutory registers of directors and shareholders at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board meeting minutes
By-laws adopted by resolution
Share certificates evidencing the subscription
Registered office and records custody acknowledgement
Bank KYC package (certificate of incorporation, NEQ extract, directors' ID, beneficial ownership declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or a counterparty queries the corporate authority, issue a certified director resolution and obtain an updated REQ extract; if the by-law adoption is challenged, formalize the by-law ratification at a subsequent board meeting and re-file the governance records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — pure equity holding SPV; no statutory industrial or operational permit required under Quebec law for passive shareholding and dividend collection activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — passive equity holding activity involves no industrial installation, contaminant discharge, or construction works triggering the EIA regime under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2), ss. 31.0.1 and 153
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the SPV's administrative operations. If a leased office is used, the lessor-tenant arrangement must respect municipal wastewater by-laws and Quebec Building Code ventilation standards. Any future acquisition of an industrial subsidiary's facility would independently require MELCCFP authorization and a cleaner production assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: if the registered office is leased, obtain a fire safety attestation from the competent municipal fire service under the Building Safety Act and applicable municipal by-laws. Structural: no load-bearing or structural inspection required for office-only administrative use. Occupational: no CNESST clearance is required for a passive holding corporation without employees; if directors or staff are later remunerated, register for source deductions with Revenu Québec and a CRA payroll account prior to hiring.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and Part I corporate income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec QST, provincial corporate income tax and related registration obligations. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec CLIC (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canada does not issue a standalone VAT TIN. The statutory corporate tax identifier is the CRA Business Number (BN), a 9-digit root with separate program accounts, such as RT for GST/HST and RP for payroll. A foreign-incorporated entity may apply for a BN by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or by using CRA's online business registration service. After incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, or after extra-provincial registration in Quebec of a federal corporation, the entity obtains a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises and registers with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial corporate tax through the CLIC portal. A non-resident corporation engaged solely in passive equity holding and receipt of dividends or capital gains is generally not required to register for GST/HST or QST, but if it is resident in Canada by incorporation or central management and control it must file Canadian and Quebec corporate income tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election or elective transparency regime exists in Canada. A Quebec business corporation is per se a taxable entity and cannot elect partnership status or disregarded-entity status. Canada's hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act, including section 18.4 and related provisions, are mandatory anti-avoidance rules that deny deduction/non-recognition mismatches; they are not elective mechanisms. Ancillary elections such as capital-dividend account or foreign-affiliate surplus elections do not alter entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT-type tax) plus Quebec QST (Quebec sales tax). For taxable supplies made in Quebec, the combined headline charge on the tax-exclusive price is GST 5% plus QST 9.975%, totaling 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies made during the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, being the GST/HST small-supplier threshold; Quebec QST uses a matching CAD 30,000 threshold. Dividends, interest, and proceeds from disposition of shares are exempt financial services under Schedule V, Part VII of the Excise Tax Act and do not count as taxable supplies, so a pure equity holding SPV normally has no mandatory GST/HST or QST registration unless it separately makes taxable commercial supplies in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, no continuous transaction control clearance platform, no API tax clearance requirement, and no digital stamping mandate. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices in verifiable formats such as XML, PDF, or EDI. The federal government is voluntarily promoting the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard based on Peppol, but adoption is not mandatory for a passive equity holding SPV.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec QST rules that mirror it, tangible personal property exported from Canada is zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods under Schedule VI, Part V and retains documentary proof of export, including customs declarations, transport documents, and evidence that possession passed outside Canada. Services supplied to non-residents may also qualify for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V if the statutory conditions are met. However, a pure equity holding SPV's dividend, interest, and capital-gain income constitutes exempt financial services under Schedule V, Part VII, not zero-rated export supplies, and the SPV cannot claim input tax credits for expenses attributable to exempt activities unless it also carries on separately taxable commercial activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A filed through the Canadian Automated Export Declaration/CAED system, including the exporter's proof number, for reportable commercial shipments)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Cargo Manifest evidencing physical export from Canada to the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank payment advice evidencing receipt of the foreign export proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list, and supply contract stating Incoterms, destination, and transfer of title to the non-resident buyer
For exported or offshore services: dated service agreement, statement of work or completion certificate, and written confirmation that the service recipient is not resident in Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec treat export zero-rating claims supported by the documented evidence bundle as a high-risk audit area. If the documentation is deficient or false, the supply will be re-characterized as taxable in Canada, GST/QST will be assessed on the full consideration, the corresponding input tax credit or rebate will be clawed back, and compound daily interest will accrue from the due date of the return. Civil penalties include a false-statement penalty under the Excise Tax Act of 25% of the understated net tax or overstated refund, a gross-negligence penalty under Income Tax Act section 163(2) of 50% of the understated income tax for knowingly or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence making a false statement, and criminal fines and imprisonment under Income Tax Act section 239 and Excise Tax Act section 285 for wilful evasion. The normal reassessment limitation period is generally four years for GST/HST, and no limitation period applies where misrepresentation is attributable to fraud, wilful default, neglect, or carelessness, permitting retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — monetary authority issuing CAD and manager of the Official International Reserves as fiscal agent of the Minister of Finance under the Bank of Canada Act and Currency Act. Canada operates a free-floating exchange-rate regime; there is no dedicated foreign-exchange control agency. OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) supervises Schedule I banks prudentially, while FINTRAC enforces the AML/CFT and cross-border transaction reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada complies with IMF Article VIII and maintains no capital-control approval regime: inbound equity subscriptions, dividends, intercompany loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds are freely remittable in CAD or foreign currency without central-bank consent. The only profit-remittance friction is fiscal: dividends paid by a Quebec-resident corporation to a non-resident attract federal Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory; treaty-reduced to 15% portfolio / 5% for a beneficial owner corporation holding at least 10% of voting shares under most Canadian treaties) plus Quebec's parallel 12% withholding under Section 1042 of the Quebec Taxation Act, with Revenu Québec generally administering treaty relief consistent with the applicable convention. Administrative compliance requires NR4 information returns and CRA remittance of Part XIII withholding by the 15th day of the following month. The Investment Canada Act net-benefit review applies to acquisitions of control of a Canadian business above monetary thresholds, but does not restrict the SPV's treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. A Quebec-resident entity may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts indefinitely in onshore or offshore accounts, subject only to FINTRAC reporting thresholds (Electronic Funds Transfer Report and Large Cash Transaction Report at CAD 10,000) and standard Canadian tax reporting (T1134/T1135 for foreign affiliates and foreign property).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + CAD Operational Account
CAD Operational Account + USD clearing sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low as primary clearing bank; Conditional as auxiliary payment rail. Canada has no 'Electronic Money Institution' licensing class; offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, Mercury) holding only foreign EMI or money-transmitter authorizations cannot operate as Schedule I deposit-taking banks, cannot clear CAD through Lynx, and cannot hold escrowed subscription proceeds for a Quebec holding company. Legal constraints: (i) any provider servicing Canadian residents must be registered with FINTRAC as a money services business under PCMLTFA and, since the Retail Payment Activities Act, 2021 regime came into force (September/November 2024), registered as a payment service provider; (ii) an unregistered foreign EMI is non-compliant for soliciting Canadian business; (iii) a foreign EMI account cannot satisfy a 'capital escrow' undertaking demanded by the parent or downstream lenders. Use such rails only for discretionary expense disbursements; never for structured equity or debt-covenant legs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandatory. FINTRAC's Client Identification Standard permits remote onboarding through the dual-process method, credit-file verification, or attestation by a regulated third party (lawyer, notary, or accountant) who performs face-to-face identity verification. In Quebec practice, however, a non-resident-owned passive SPV in the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier will ordinarily require: (i) a certified attestation from the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) dated within 30 days; (ii) notarized passports of directors and of all individuals with significant control; (iii) a video-call interview with the relationship manager or in-person verification by a Quebec notary/lawyer acting as introducer; and (iv) appointment of a Quebec-resident authorized signatory or service-of-process agent. A fully remote opening without any Canadian professional introducer is rarely granted and may take 2 to 8 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) domiciled in a medium/high-risk or opaque jurisdiction, with a mismatch between declared net worth and the size of the inbound capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for each UBO; certified source-of-wealth statement prepared by an external accountant or lawyer; audited financial statements of the remitting shareholder; banking reference letter from the remitting bank addressed to the Canadian bank; an ownership chain chart extending to natural persons; PEP and sanctions screening clearance output.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Quebec holdco with no employees, no physical office, no prior tax filings, and no operational history ('shell' red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: QBCA certificate of incorporation; REQ attestation of registration; register of directors and register of individuals with significant control; board resolution designating the account purpose and authorized signatories; executed corporate-services agreement with a Quebec law or accounting firm; first-year business plan and cash-flow forecast demonstrating the passive equity-holding function; CRA and Revenu Quebec business number confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment counterparties, remitters, or beneficiaries located in sanctions-affected, non-cooperative, or non-SWIFT jurisdictions, or reliance on unregulated fintech corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy restricting counterparty rails to regulated banks; executed commercial documents or legal opinion establishing the economic substance of each flow; bank sanctions-screening output showing no alerts; FINTRAC registration certificate of any non-bank processor; CRS/FATCA tax-transparency certifications for the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the stated passive-holding purpose and actual account activity — repetitive large wires, round-tripping, rapid in-and-out movements, or unexplained same-day reversals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved transaction matrix (counterparty types, amounts, frequency) agreed with the relationship manager; investment and loan documentation underlying each transfer; board resolutions authorizing each disbursement; monthly reconciliation and source-of-funds records; annual compliance confirmation letter submitted to the bank's AML officer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., the 60th day following a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties are assessed by the REQ; persistent failure to file annual declarations, generally for two consecutive years, triggers a notice and administrative strike-off/dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA annual return (if the SPV is a Canada Business Corporations Act company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the filing of articles of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Director may issue a notice of default and, if the default is not cured, administratively dissolve the corporation; no separate late-filing fee is imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 corporation income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each taxation year (e.g., June 30 following a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalties apply as a percentage of any unpaid balance plus monthly interest accrual; a zero-income equity-holding SPV still must file to avoid administrative assessments and loss of attribute carry-forwards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the taxation year, generally matching the federal T2 deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec imposes interest and parallel late-filing penalties; failure to file may lead to administrative assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and CBCA, an auditor is mandatory unless all shareholders unanimously waive the auditor by written resolution and the corporation is not a reporting/distributing issuer. There is no asset/revenue small-company audit threshold; a single-shareholder pure equity-holding SPV may pass the waiver each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for non-public private enterprises; IFRS (Part I) applies to reporting issuers or where voluntarily elected. A pure equity-holding subsidiary generally prepares ASPE financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration is the annual confirmation and update mechanism for ultimate beneficial ownership information. Share transfers must be recorded in the corporate share register and, where UBO details change, the REQ file must be amended within 30 days. If the SPV is a CBCA corporation, an individual-with-significant-control (ISC) register must be maintained and updated within 15 days of learning of any change; this register is kept on site and is not separately filed with a government authority.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book containing resolutions and meeting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–900 per year for Quebec registered office/registered agent services, including annual-declaration monitoring and corporate records support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution; otherwise USD 3,000–8,000 for a certified audit of a simple equity-holding SPV under ASPE

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal + 11.5% Quebec = 26.5% combined general corporate rate (CCPC small business rate 9%/3.2% not available on passive investment income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Intercorporate dividend deduction (s.112(1) ITA): dividends from taxable Canadian corporations are excluded from taxable income; foreign affiliate dividend exemption (s.113 ITA); RDTOH refund mechanism returns Part IV tax when dividends are distributed; effective rate on pure dividend holding income ≈ 0%; Quebec's refundable tax on dividends does not apply to intercorporate dividends (redundancy: the QRD is for individuals).
